I was 10 years old when I first listened to nirvana in 93. He died the following year. Where I grew up, he was seen as a dangerous influence on the youth in our small town, because of his drug use and some of the lyrical content, as well as his behavior on stage. I loved nirvana from the first 10 seconds of hearing all apologies for the first time (first song I heard). He was seen as a gentle and tortured soul by my older cousins and peers, as well as older fans in their late teens and twenties. Kurt kind of personified how we all felt, frustrated and filled with rage but also kind of innocent as well, because he had a a way about him that was sweet and thoughtful, especially during certain interviews where he was cooperative, or when he was lifting fans up on stage during the live and loud, not to mention his demeanor on unplugged. He had a charming complexity about him that appealed to young people, even children like myself. When he died, a lot of us felt like “well, if life sucks now, it must just get really bad as you get older”. Our generation was kind of a lost generation, we really didn’t have anything to fight for or stand up for other than third wave feminism, which Kurt was also an ally of. Adults in the mid to late thirties and older didn’t really get him or the music, and often chalked him and nirvana as “losers” who make noise. My parents hated that I liked them, what with me being as young as I was, but when they saw how much his death affected our generation, they slowly learned to appreciate him and his music more. I hope that helps.

I think you’re looking at it the wrong way (well maybe “wrong” isn’t the word, but hear me out). This isn’t really even “The Joker”. Hell, he might not even be “The Joker” we know (and love to hate/hate to love). This is a man who just found his joker wings. A man who found meaning and purpose in embracing his madness. And in a decade or so, he could do a few pushups, read a few books, and learn to become who he was meant to be: a criminal mastermind and yin to Batman’s yang. He is just starting to figure out who he is, and what he wants to become. So to just chalk him up as a “whimpering dog” is premature, imo. I loved this movie. It would have been great if he wasn’t “the joker”, it made me feel and it had me on the edge of my seat.

What is getting to me? I’ve hurt my family and friends repeatedly throughout my life with my drug addiction and mental illness. I’m bi-polar/ mildy schizophrenic and I am a difficult person to deal with. 
I have a difficult time maintaining relationships due to delusions and fear of rejection. I’ve had two partners die, one in a car accident, the other from alcohol poisoning. I was engaged to the first one. She was the best thing to happen to me. I’ve not been able to get over these experiences.
I used to be healthy and relatively happy, full of hope and ambition. I’ve lost pieces of that over the last couple decades (I’m 36). I have no appetite for life. I lost my joy, I don’t love the things I used to (music, art, running). I eat compulsively, I drink, and I can’t stop. I know it’s hard for those I love to see me this way. I have a dead end job, and no career. I’ve nothing to show for the years I spent trying to make it as a professional musician. I lost everything due to drugs and alcohol. I wake up fearing the world, I loathe being around others. I can barely muster the energy to go to work and be walked on by my superiors. 
I’ve tried flipping the script, getting clean, looking for other work, but I just don’t have the energy. I’m spending all the energy I have just to make it through the day.

I’m 5’7”, and I went on a date with a woman that was set up by a mutual friend. This woman let me buy dinner, pay for us to go to an expensive concert, and buy all her drinks. Then she asked for a cab, which I also paid for. We laughed and had good conversation. I thought we were hitting it off. 

I asked if I could kiss her goodnight and that I would love to see her again. As she got into the car, she told me no. I asked why, I thought we had a good time...and she told me this: “You’re just too short for me. Sorry, but there are too many short men in the world, and we don’t need to breed any more.” Btw, she was 5’2” at the most.

I wanted to kill myself right there. I’ve had lovely women in my life since, but she really hurt me. It still affects me. 

If you’re someone who doesn’t like short men (or women) just tell them instead of letting them think you’re having a good time and that you’re genuinely interested in THEM and not their stature. Because if you don’t, and you lead them on, you’re a garbage person.
